channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Canada Unemployment Rate forecast to remain unchanged in June
item.description: Markets are anticipating a fairly stable report when Statistics Canada releases its Labour Force Survey on Friday. While the Net Change in Employment is predicted to rise by 10K in June, adding to the 87.8K gain in May, the Unemployment Rate is forecast to stay at 6.6%.

item.title: Euro retraces previous gains as Eurozone data paves the way for an ECB pause
item.description: The Euro (EUR) has given away most of the daily gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, returning to the 1.1430 area from session highs at 1.1475, which leaves the pair practically flat on the daily chart.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD turns upside down amid renewed Middle East hostilities
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) surrenders its early gains and slides 0.73% to near $59.50 during the European trading session on Friday. The white metal turns negative amid fears that the next monetary policy move by the Federal Reserve (Fed) will be on the upside.

item.title: Australian Dollar rises on hawkish RBA, Iran diplomacy pressures USD
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.6950 on Friday at the time of writing, up 0.10% on the day after reaching a more than two-week high earlier in the day. The pair gives back part of its gains as investors remain caught between a weaker US Dollar (USD) and lingering factors supporting the Greenback.

item.title: Gold heads for weekly loss as Middle East tensions, Fed hike fears cap recovery
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades on the back foot on Friday, struggling to build on the previous day's gains and heading for a weekly loss as renewed hostilities in the Middle East have revived fears of energy-driven inflation and Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hikes.

item.title: Euro: Range-bound rebound faces key resistance against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux notes EUR/USD has rebounded after forming an interim low near 1.1325 and moved back into its prior range, signalling limited follow-through on the earlier breakdown.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Softer Canada jobs seen weigh against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad describes USD/CAD trading just below 1.4200 and broadly aligned with US-Canada two-year yield spreads ahead of June labor data.

item.title: "The bar for a material hawkish turn is high": ING says the Bank of Canada won't surprise next week
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) is outperforming the US Dollar in the short term, pulling the USD/CAD pair down from recent multi-month highs. This corrective move comes at a crucial juncture, as global markets look ahead to the Bank of Canada's (BoC) upcoming policy meeting.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD wavers around $4,100 with the bearish trend intact
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) nurses minor losses with price action contained within Thursday’s trading range, around the $4,100 level, set for 1.6% weekly depreciation. Precious metals struggled this week as the resumption of hostilities in Iran boosted Oil prices, pressuring central banks to hike interest rates.

item.title: Indian Rupee gives back gains as US Dollar recovers
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) gives back its early gains against the US Dollar (USD) in India's afternoon trading hours on Friday.

item.title: Euro declines as cooling Eurozone inflation, Japan pension reforms lift Yen
item.description: EUR/JPY trades around 184.95 on Friday at the time of writing, down 0.35% on the day, as the Japanese Yen (JPY) benefits from renewed demand following the government's announcement of a potential shift toward greater domestic investment.

item.title: Gold: Tentative stabilisation on oil relief – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Christopher Wong and Sim Moh Siong highlight that Gold has rebounded as Oil prices eased, reducing inflation and Fed tightening concerns, while a softer US Dollar also supported the move.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar eases from three-week highs near 0.5800 as the US Dollar bounces up
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is giving away gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, trading at the 0.5775 area after hitting fresh three-week highs at 0.5794 earlier on the day.

item.title: US Dollar: Geopolitics faded as markets eye rates – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes the US Dollar (USD) has been broadly unchanged despite renewed Middle East tensions, as Oil has retraced and risk sentiment improved.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $59.47 per troy ounce, down 0.86% from the $59.98 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Firmer against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists highlight that USD/CAD is tactically expensive versus the 2-year spread and has recently met resistance near 1.4250 before retracing toward 1.4130.

item.title: BoJ will likely revise 2026 GDP forecast higher in Q2 report
item.description: According to sources, the Bank of Japan (BoJ) may revise up the fiscal 2026 economic growth forecast in the quarterly report due in July. The BoJ is expected to report that it will keep focus on the risk of inflation overshooting the central bank’s target, Reuters reports.

item.title: Euro: Yield spreads hint at recovery against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny highlights that European Central Bank (ECB) minutes added little new information but confirmed openness to another rate hike, consistent with MUFG’s call for a 25bp move in September.

item.title: British Pound retreats sharply from January 2008 highs amid broad-based JPY rally
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross attracted heavy selling on Friday, snapping a two-day winning streak to the highest level since January 2008, around the 218.00 mark set the previous day.

item.title: British Pound surrenders early gains as US Dollar regains ground
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) gives back its early gains and turns almost flat around 1.3410 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Friday.

item.title: Federal Reserve: No near-term hikes signalled – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Christoph Balz and Bernd Weidensteiner interpret recent data and Fed communications as pointing to stable policy rates in coming months.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Dollar finds resistance at the 161.75 previous support
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) holds losses below 161.75 against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on Friday following a 100-pip reversal earlier on the day.

item.title: Gold seems vulnerable near $4,100 as USD rebounds amid Fed hike bets and Iran risks
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) touches a fresh low during the first half of the European session on Friday, with bears looking to extend the intraday descent further below the $4,100 mark.

item.title: Equities: Risk of renewed rates volatility – BNY
item.description: BNY strategist David Tam warns that a renewed rise in rates volatility, as measured by the MOVE Index, could pressure U.S. equities, particularly technology and growth segments. He says investors may need to reduce equity exposure, shorten portfolio equity duration and favor defensive sectors.

item.title: IEA confirms: Oil demand to rise by 1.2M bpd YoY in Q4
item.description: According to the latest forecast from the International Energy Agency (IEA), the global Oil demand will rise by 1.2 million barrels per day (bpd) Year-on-Year (YoY) in the last quarter of this year.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Jobs and BoC caution shape outlook – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole highlights that Canada’s June jobs report is expected to show a sharp slowdown in hiring and a pickup in wage growth. He argues the bar for a hawkish shift by the Bank of Canada (BoC) remains high, with benign inflation and USMCA-related risks limiting hike prospects.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Recovers from three-week low; flat above 1.4150 ahead of jobs data
item.description: The USD/CAD pair stages a modest intraday recovery from the 1.4135 area, or a three-week low touched this Friday, and climbs to the top end of its daily range during the early European session.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy shift talk supports JPY – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny notes the Japanese Yen is leading G10 gains after Finance Minister Katayama unexpectedly urged households and the GPIF to increase investments in Japanese financial assets.

item.title: Japan’s Kihara says that specifics of monetary policy to be left to BoJ
item.description: Japan’s Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said during the European trading session on Friday that the specifics of monetary policy to be left to the Bank of Japan (BoJ).

item.title: Euro remains pinned at one-year lows against the British Pound as Euro Area inflation moderates
item.description: The Euro (EUR) remains on the defensive against the British Pound (GBP) on Friday, with the EUR/GBP pair unable to take off from one-year lows at the 0.8515 area. Data from Germany and France confirmed that inflationary pressures moderated in June, which added pressure on the common currency.
